verses.text: Darius decided to appoint one hundred twenty governors to rule throughout his kingdom.
Over them he put three officials, and Daniel was one of them. The governors reported to these officials, so that the king would not suffer any loss.
Daniel stood out above the other officials and governors because he had an excellent spirit. So the king planned to put him in charge of the whole kingdom.

Then the other officials and governors tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel handled the kingdom's affairs. But they could not find any wrongdoing or fault in him, because he was trustworthy. He was never careless or dishonest.
Finally these men said, "We will never find anything to accuse this Daniel of, unless it has to do with the law of his God."
So these officials and governors went together to the king and said, "May King Darius live forever!

All the officials of the kingdom, the leaders, the governors, the advisers, and the rulers have agreed that the king should issue an order and enforce it: for the next thirty days, anyone who prays to any god or human except you, Your Majesty, will be thrown into the lions' den.
Now, Your Majesty, issue the order and sign it in writing, so that it cannot be changed. That way it will follow the law of the Medes and Persians, which can never be cancelled."
So King Darius signed the written order.

When Daniel learned that the order had been signed, he went home to his upstairs room, where the windows opened toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his God, just as he had always done.
Then these men went as a group and found Daniel praying and asking his God for help.

So they went to the king and spoke to him about his order: "Didn't you sign an order that for the next thirty days anyone who prays to any god or human except you, Your Majesty, will be thrown into the lions' den?" The king answered, "That is true. It follows the law of the Medes and Persians, which can never be cancelled."
Then they said to the king, "Daniel, one of the captives from Judah, pays no attention to you, Your Majesty, or to the order you signed. He still prays three times a day."
When the king heard this, he was very upset. He was determined to save Daniel, and he tried everything he could until sunset to rescue him.
Then the men went as a group to the king and said, "Remember, Your Majesty, that by the law of the Medes and Persians, no order or law the king issues can be changed."
So the king gave the order, and Daniel was brought and thrown into the lions' den. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you always serve, rescue you!"
A stone was brought and placed over the opening of the den. The king sealed it with his own signet ring and the rings of his nobles, so that nothing could be done to change Daniel's situation.
Then the king went back to his palace and spent the night without eating. He refused any entertainment, and he could not sleep.
At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the lions' den.
When he came near the den, he called out to Daniel in a worried voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you always serve, been able to rescue you from the lions?"
Daniel answered, "May the king live forever!
My God sent his angel, and he shut the lions' mouths. They have not hurt me, because I was found innocent in God's sight. And I have never done anything wrong to you, Your Majesty."
The king was overjoyed and ordered that Daniel be lifted out of the den. When Daniel was lifted out, no wound of any kind was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

Then at the king's command, the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought and thrown into the lions' den, along with their wives and children. Before they reached the floor of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to the people of every nation and language in all the world: "May you have great peace!

"I order that in every part of my kingdom people must tremble with fear before the God of Daniel. For he is the living God, and he lasts forever. His kingdom will never be destroyed. His rule will never end.
He rescues and he saves. He does signs and wonders in heaven and on earth. He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions."
So Daniel did well during the rule of Darius and the rule of Cyrus the Persian.
